overall_reason: The page barely moves: four of five measured controls changed instantly, and the one movement is a 2 px lift with a shadow on a tool card over 150 ms on Tailwind's default curve, which is a stock hover signal rather than a designed system.

score.reason: T-PURPOSE and T-FREQUENCY pass because controls answer instantly, but T-MOTION-SYSTEM finds only Tailwind default timing and T-HOVER-SIGNAL finds the stock card lift.

findings.title: Hover answers with one small signal
findings.where: tool cards on the "Browse all tools" view (trigger t1, card 395 x 263 px), 1440
findings.evidence: The motion table measured translate and box-shadow over 150 ms on cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) with 2 px travel; the stylesheet declares ".hover:-translate-y-0.5:hover", so every card lifts the same way. The lift still moves 2 px under reduced motion.
findings.before: Every tool card lifts 2 px and gains a shadow on hover.
findings.after: Keep one signal for the card, such as a border or title colour change, and drop the lift.
findings.why: The same lift and shadow on every card is the stock card-kit hover and adds nothing a colour change would not.

findings.title: One curve family and one duration scale
findings.evidence: All 3 transitioning elements at 1440 (the buttons "Get started", "Find my AI stack" and "Browse all tools") use Tailwind's default cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) at 150 ms, and the sweep's MOT-001 hit records ".transition-all". No motion tokens are declared.
findings.before: Framework default timing with no system behind it.
findings.after: Name one easing and one or two duration steps as tokens and transition named properties only.
findings.why: With so little motion this costs little, but the timing is the framework's rather than a decision.

strengths: The nav buttons and "Find my AI stack" change state instantly, which suits a tool a visitor operates.
The page runs no load animations and no loops (0 keyframes, no running animations).
